releases.notes:
- Store: add your own stores (.unistore) by QR code or link, see every entry a store offers, and install right after opening it (it no longer waits for the console's apps to be checked); zips unpack much faster.
- Files: select several items to copy, move, install or delete at once; big folders are deleted faster.
- Game mods: Cleanup lists the LayeredFS mods in /luma/titles and whether their game is installed, and deleting a game offers to delete its mods too.
- Music: the player keeps playing in the background after B, jumps instantly within an MP3 and can repeat the list or one track.
- FTP: FileZilla no longer waits 20 s before each transfer; transfers over FTP and the web page show their progress on the console, and the web page's address shows as a QR code.
- Every list sorts both ways, filters are icons, every grid has a tile size, and downloads start sooner on an Old 3DS.

- Store: the date each app was last updated shows on its card, a new filter keeps only apps updated in the last month, 6 months or year, and choosing the same sort again turns it round (oldest first, Z to A...).
- Store: the categories in the filter are icons now, with their name when you point at them.
- Fixed: NSA could crash when it restarted after an update while the Store was open.
- Fixed: the main menu's hint showed in English without its button, and Settings' volume hint was not translated.

- New Store: browse Universal-DB's homebrew with icons, search and filters, install the CIA or download the 3DSX (also the apps that come in a .zip or .7z, on Old 3DS and 2DS too), and see what is already on the console.
- A guide shows how NSA works with short tours on the real screens: you do each step yourself. Later versions offer only what is new (Settings -> Guide replays any chapter).
- The main menu is yours: tiles and a row of icons that you can reorder by dragging them or hide, and the focus slides along with your finger.
- NSA's own on-screen keyboard everywhere: searches, names and URLs.
- Long messages scroll above their buttons, a turning wheel shows while something loads, and everything new speaks all 11 languages.

- The Store follows each app's own install steps, as Universal-Updater does: apps that come in a .zip or .7z now install or download too (3D Pinball, 3DS Quick Reboot, mGBA and others).
- Downloading a .3dsx from the Store asks only yes or no and saves it in /3ds/, without the CIA choices.
- The author's note before installing reads as one paragraph, without lines cut in the middle.

- The Store, the guide, menu editing and the rest of what came in 0.8 now speak all 11 languages (until now only English and Spanish).
- Fixed: NSA froze at start in Simplified Chinese once its font gained the new characters.

- New Store: browse Universal-DB's homebrew, with icons, search and filters, and install the CIA or download the 3DSX; a mark shows what is already on the console.
- A guide shows how NSA works with short tours on the real screens: you do each step yourself. Later versions offer only what is new (Settings -> Guide replays any chapter).
- The main menu is yours: tiles and a row of icons that you can reorder by dragging them, and the focus slides along with your finger.
- NSA's own on-screen keyboard everywhere: searches, names and URLs.
- Long messages scroll above their buttons, and a turning wheel shows while something loads.

- Fixed a bug when the console was suspended: after closing the lids or pressing HOME, NSA lost the Wi-Fi for good, the FTP and web servers never came back, and HOME could freeze the console until a restart. Both now work again after waking.
- Import PKSM's and JKSM's backups next to NSA's and Checkpoint's, with their own badges (JKSM also from /JKSV).
- The web page can answer the console's questions (confirmations and choices) from the computer.
- Progress shows two decimals (42.57 %), and the 3D depth is gentler.
- Fixed installing from a URL, QR code or History: the confirmation question overwrote the address, so every download with one link failed at once ("curl 3").

- NSA speaks 11 languages, chosen from a list in Settings: English, Spanish, Catalan, French, German, Italian, Portuguese, Russian, Japanese and Chinese (simplified and traditional); "System" follows the console's own.
- Receiving from another 3DS asks in a list (Install now, Save, Reject...) that says what each choice does, and the top screen shows who sends and where it is saved; whole folders can be sent too. Sending to another 3DS needs this version on both consoles.
- Installing from a URL or QR asks how (Install, Save and install, Save, install and delete, or Save); Dropbox and Google Drive links work, and links and names show whole, with %20 and the like turned into characters, also in History.
- Faster downloads, FTP and sends to another 3DS, one transfer at a time and a steady speed.
- The web page gains a System tab (console, network, storage, battery), plays the console's music, groups updates and DLC under their game, and shows transfers as a toast.
- Back arrows in Settings, Remote install and the changelog; the music no longer pauses for FTP unless you ask (an Old 3DS is asked once).

- NSA speaks 11 languages, chosen from a list in Settings: English, Spanish, Catalan, French, German, Italian, Portuguese, Russian, Japanese and Chinese (simplified and traditional); "System" follows the console's own.
- The web page gains a System tab (console, network, storage, battery), plays the console's music, groups updates and DLC under their game, remembers the titles' names and icons, and shows transfers as a toast.
- Installing from a URL or QR asks how (Install, Save and install, Save, install and delete, or Save); Dropbox and Google Drive links work.
- Faster downloads, FTP and sends to another 3DS, one transfer at a time and a steady speed; whole folders can be sent. Sending to another 3DS needs this version on both consoles.
- Back arrows in Settings, Remote install and the changelog; the music no longer pauses for FTP unless you ask (an Old 3DS is asked once).
